description:
HadOM3 is the ocean component of HadCM3 and was designed specifically to achieve a stable, realistic coupled climate simulation without flux adjustments. The model uses a regular latitude–longitude grid with a horizontal resolution of 1.25° × 1.25° and 20 vertical levels. It simulates realistic representations of major current systems and ocean heat transport, which was one of the key reasons HadCM3 could maintain a stable climate without artificial corrections. The ocean grid is carefully aligned with the atmospheric grid to simplify coupling, and the ocean model is integrated with a 1 hour time step. During coupling, atmospheric fluxes of heat, freshwater and momentum are accumulated over a day and then applied to the ocean, after which ocean feedbacks are returned to the atmosphere.

HadOM3 treated subgrid-scale mixing and tracer transport using the Gent–McWilliams eddy parameterization, which represents the effects of unresolved mesoscale ocean eddies through an isopycnal transport scheme. This reduced systematic biases in sea-surface temperatures and helped reproduce observed meridional ocean heat transports in both hemispheres. The model was also coupled to a thermodynamic–dynamic sea-ice scheme, allowing exchanges of heat and freshwater associated with ice formation and melt.
